Identity.History: Athens became one of the leading city-states of classical Greece, renowned for democracy, naval power, trade, philosophy, and the arts. After helping defeat Persia in the Greco-Persian Wars, it built the Delian League into a maritime empire. Rivalry with Sparta led to the Peloponnesian War and eventual defeat in 404 BC. Athens later recovered influence, but never regained the dominance of its 5th-century golden age.
